## Prototype Dual-Metric Sweep

This is a lightweight prototype to compare metric behavior before wiring full Snakemake inference.

```{python}
#| label: prototype-sweep
def simple_kernel(beta: float, kmax: int) -> np.ndarray:
    nu = np.arange(1, kmax + 1, dtype=float)
    return 1.0 - (1.0 - beta) ** nu


def beta_from_r0(r0: float, gamma: float, avg_degree: float) -> float:
    return float(np.clip((r0 * gamma) / avg_degree, 1e-6, 1.0 - 1e-6))


def mix_kernels_blockwise(
    n: int,
    kmax: int,
    omega: float,
    c1: np.ndarray,
    c2: np.ndarray,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> np.ndarray:
    kernels = np.zeros((n, kmax), dtype=float)
    split = n // 2
    draws = rng.random(n)
    for i in range(n):
        if i < split:
            kernels[i] = c1 if draws[i] >= omega else c2
        else:
            kernels[i] = c2 if draws[i] >= omega else c1
    return kernels


def fit_best_simple_beta(kernel: np.ndarray, grid_size: int = 2000) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray]:
    k = kernel.shape[0]
    beta_grid = np.linspace(1e-6, 1.0 - 1e-6, grid_size)
    nu = np.arange(1, k + 1, dtype=float)
    candidates = 1.0 - np.power((1.0 - beta_grid[:, None]), nu[None, :])
    l1 = np.mean(np.abs(candidates - kernel[None, :]), axis=1)
    idx = int(np.argmin(l1))
    beta_hat = float(beta_grid[idx])
    return beta_hat, candidates[idx]


N = 256
AVG_DEGREE = 18
GAMMA = 0.1
R0_1 = 1.0
OMEGA = 0.0
SEED = 37

EPSILONS = np.round(np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 10), 2)
R0_2S = np.round(np.linspace(1.1, 4.0, 20), 2)

rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
rows = []

for epsilon in EPSILONS:
    A = np.asarray(sbm(N, AVG_DEGREE, float(epsilon), seed=SEED))
    kmax = int(np.max(A.sum(axis=1)))
    beta1 = beta_from_r0(R0_1, GAMMA, AVG_DEGREE)

    for r0_2 in R0_2S:
        beta2 = beta_from_r0(float(r0_2), GAMMA, AVG_DEGREE)
        c1 = simple_kernel(beta1, kmax)
        c2 = simple_kernel(beta2, kmax)

        kernel_samples = mix_kernels_blockwise(
            n=N,
            kmax=kmax,
            omega=OMEGA,
            c1=c1,
            c2=c2,
            rng=rng,
        )
        kernel_mean = kernel_samples.mean(axis=0)

        beta_hat, kernel_fit = fit_best_simple_beta(kernel_mean)
        l1_complexity = float(np.mean(np.abs(kernel_mean - kernel_fit)))

        rho_samples = np.full(kernel_samples.shape[0], beta_hat, dtype=float)
        _, _, malahbois_lambda, _ = compute_mahalanobis_decomposed(kernel_samples, rho_samples)

        rows.append(
            {
                "epsilon": float(epsilon),
                "R0_2": float(r0_2),
                "kmax": kmax,
                "l1_complexity": l1_complexity,
                "malahbois_complexity": float(malahbois_lambda),
            }
        )

df_metrics = pd.DataFrame(rows)
df_metrics.head()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-dual-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Prototype heatmaps comparing L1 and Malahbois complexity over epsilon and R0_2."
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5), constrained_layout=True)

sns.heatmap(
    df_metrics.pivot(index="R0_2", columns="epsilon", values="l1_complexity"),
    cmap="viridis",
    ax=axes[0],
)
axes[0].set_title("L1 Complexity")
axes[0].set_xlabel(r"$\epsilon$")
axes[0].set_ylabel(r"$R_0^{(2)}$")

sns.heatmap(
    df_metrics.pivot(index="R0_2", columns="epsilon", values="malahbois_complexity"),
    cmap="magma",
    ax=axes[1],
)
axes[1].set_title("Malahbois Complexity (lambda)")
axes[1].set_xlabel(r"$\epsilon$")
axes[1].set_ylabel(r"$R_0^{(2)}$")
```
